content:
alex: Heads-up — running into a structured-output mismatch in the Python SDK when the model's tool response includes extra keys. Anyone run into this recently?

meenal: Yep. We saw this yesterday with the analyzer tool. SDK casting to the typed dataclass strips unknown fields by default. End result: useful metadata (meta/trace) is lost.

alex: Minimal repro I pushed to my sandbox: the model func_call returns a dict like {"result": ..., "meta": { ... }} but the SDK returns only the typed fields.

alex: Repro snippet:
```python
resp = client.func_call(name="analyzer", input={"text":"foo"})
# expected: resp.structured == {'result': '...', 'meta': {...}}
# actual: resp.structured == {'result': '...'}  # meta dropped
```

ryan: Is this the pydantic/default dataclass extras/ignore behavior? I think pydantic models ignore extras unless configured with Extra.allow. Is the SDK coercing into an internal model?

sara: Exactly. Python SDK currently coerces into our generated TypedOutput dataclass which uses pydantic BaseModel with default config. Other language SDKs behave differently — e.g., Go returns a raw map for unknowns, Rust preserves unknown fields in a Value.

alex: Proposal: add an opt-in flag on func_call: `preserve_unknown_fields=True` which would keep an additional `resp.raw_structured` (dict) alongside the typed object. Default should remain False to avoid surprising typed consumers.

meenal: Alternative (no API surface change): expose the raw payload under `resp._raw` already present in the transport layer. Consumers could opt in to read that. But that's not documented and feels hacky.

devex-bot: FYI — filed RFC: rfc/2026-struct-preserve (link: https://redwood.example/rfc/2026).

alex: For streaming toolcall responses: another gotcha — partial JSON arrives across multiple chunks, and our current incremental parser fails on nested objects. We end up returning truncated parsed objects.

ryan: Right now we buffer until we see a matching close brace '}' or end-of-stream. That's brittle for nested structures or when the model emits extraneous text. I suggest using an incremental JSON decoder (e.g., ijson or JSONDecoder.raw_decode) to safely parse prefixes.

sara: For a quick mitigation I can add a fallback: if parsing fails on stream frames, emit the raw text as `resp.stream_text` and mark `parsed=False` in the event. That way callers can decide to reparse. Tests should include fragmented JSON across frames.

alex: Sounds good. Also let's add a one-time-per-session warn log when we fall back so we can find customers hitting this in prod.

meenal: I'll add an integration test: replay a model trace that returns `{"result":..., "meta": {"x": 1}}` split across frames, assert `stream_text` present and that `preserve_unknown_fields` (if enabled) yields raw meta.

ryan: Another piece: auth/scoped tokens. We saw a case where dedicated tokens with limited scopes cause the API to return an anonymized response (meta removed server-side). That looks like a server masking issue, not SDK. Ping infra.

alex: Good catch — opening infra issue and linking the integration test.

alex: Action items: @sara to draft Python PR for `preserve_unknown_fields` and streaming fallback + tests. @meenal to add integration test and CI replay. @ryan to prototype incremental parse util. I'll open the infra ticket for masking.

sara: Picking this up. Quick Q: for the PR do we want `resp.raw_structured` as a top-level attr or a namespaced `resp._internal.raw_structured`? I'd prefer explicit top-level so it's easy for users.

alex: Top-level is fine if we document it. Add a deprecation plan if we ever want to change.

deploy-bot: staging build #2456 queued for sandboxes.

meenal: I'll attach logs from the failing replay once CI runs.

alex: Thanks team — ping me if you need pairing. Will follow up on the RFC comments this afternoon.

sara: ETA for PR: EOD Tue.

ryan: I'll post a tiny prototype helper for streaming JSON parse tomorrow morning.

alex: Closing loop: adding a short note to the SDK changelog draft about the new flag + streaming fallback behavior so product docs can mention it.

infra: Thx for the tag — I'm looking into whether the masking is intentional by policy or a bug. Will report back.
